answer: AI economies resist Sybil attacks via economic staking. Each agent must stake native tokens to establish identity and gain participation rights. An attacker attempting to forge numerous fake identities must acquire and lock equivalent collateral for each, making mass-scale attacks prohibitively costly. This economic burden ensures that creating a hundred fake agents on a digital knoll would require an investment as substantial as trying to capture a zephyr, quickly rendering such efforts economically unsustainable.
